messages:
Marta: Heads-up — Acme is seeing a p99 latency surge and intermittent 503s since ~04:10 UTC. They attached an error: "runtime: out of memory allocating KV cache slab". customer notes spike correlates with longer inputs and batch sizes.
Ken: Thanks, adding eng-runtime. Do we have repro traces + pod logs? Any recent rollout? :eyes:
Marta: No rollout on our side. I pulled a short log snippet from their request id 9f3a: `gpu-err OOM KV_ALLOC_FAIL slab=24MB tenant=acme-route`. Stack looks like KV allocator failing then backpressure -> slow path.
Li: paging in — looks like classic fragmentation + KV growth. Which model and quantization? Also need the heap maps: `/proc/meminfo` + `nvidia-smi topo` + runtime logs.
Marta: Model: open-llama-30b-fp16, quant=4bit-q, route tags: chat+rerank, tenant is high-concurrency. They say their typical seq len is 1024 but had bursts up to 4096.
Ken: That burst pattern can blow up KV usage. Short-term mitigation: 1) set per-tenant max_seq=2048, 2) enable KV-eviction-by-age for that route, 3) pin them to a compute pool with larger slab config. Can we apply these as a hotfix?
Li: Agree. Also recommend `allocator.tune(fract=0.75, slab_goal=32MB)` as a quick test on staging. For production, we should avoid live allocator changes without a canary.
Marta: I've notified Acme about temp limits. They accepted lowering max_seq. Applying KV eviction policy now.
infra-bot: deploy: rolling update started for runtime-pool-12 (owner: ken). CI passed.
Ken: After applying TTL-based eviction and lowering seq, we saw p95 drop from 520ms -> 220ms in internal sim. But p99 still at ~1.2s on some requests. Need full repro to iterate.
Marta: Attached a minimal repro script the customer used: `for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s -X POST /gen -d @big_prompt.json; done` with big_prompt length 3500 tokens.
Li: Repro looks heavy. Suggest reproduce in our staging with same batch concurrency and seq len. Also capture `jemalloc stats` & `nvtop` while running. Key signals: KV slab eviction rate, allocator free list growth, GPU memory fragmentation.
Ken: If fragmentation is root cause, long-term mitigations: 1) KV compaction job (offline) to free stale keys, 2) change slab allocator to prefer larger contiguous blocks, 3) route-level circuit breaker to prefer quantized smaller-model fallback.
Marta: For immediate customer relief we offered three options: (A) keep temp max_seq=2048 + eviction, (B) upgrade to dedicated pool with higher slab quota, (C) short-term rate limit. They chose A + we'll monitor.
Li: Action items: li -> run staging repro & collect jemalloc + nvml traces (ETA 2h). ken -> roll canary with allocator.tune on a single host (ETA 1h). marta -> update ticket and confirm customer still OK with limits.
Ken: Also logging note: add metric `kv.slab_fragmentation_ratio` + alert if >0.6 for 5m. We'll want rolling window alerts to catch slow regressions.
Marta: Customer update: after limits applied, errors fell to 0 and p99 improved but occasional spikes remain. They asked about root cause timeline and whether this will recur.
Li: Likely combination: longer-than-expected sequences exposing a slow KV growth bug combined with slab fragmentation from prior churn. We'll prioritize a repro to prove hypothesis. If confirmed, we'll schedule an allocator change + migration plan.
Ken: I'll own the canary and the `kv.slab_fragmentation_ratio` metric. Li owns the repro and jemalloc traces. Marta will keep the customer loop.
Marta: Thanks all — keeping ticket Z-8942 open and noting these actions. Will post results from staging here. :thumbsup:
